concept_mcqs.stem:
You run this call from Account A (111122223333):
```bash
aws sts assume-role \
  --role-arn arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/Deploy \
  --role-session-name build \
  --external-id abc
```
Caller identity:
```json
{
  "UserId": "AIDA...:ci-user",
  "Account": "111122223333",
  "Arn": "arn:aws:iam::111122223333:user/ci-user"
}
```
Target role trust policy in Account B (444455556666):
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/CI"},
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole",
      "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"sts:ExternalId": "abc"}}
    }
  ]
}
```
CloudTrail shows AccessDenied on AssumeRole. Without creating new IAM entities, which change makes this succeed while keeping least privilege?
options: Keep the trust policy as-is and add `--source-identity ci-user` to the CLI call.
Attach an inline policy to the target role granting it `"Action": "sts:AssumeRole"` on itself.
concept_mcqs.explanation: AssumeRole authorization is controlled by the target role's trust policy. The caller is a user, but the trust allows only a role principal. Changing the Principal to the exact user ARN authorizes the caller with least privilege and matches the external ID requirement.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B: The role’s permissions policy does not control who can assume it; the trust policy does. C: `--source-identity` tags the session but does not satisfy the trust Principal mismatch. D: Trusting the account root would work but is broader than necessary and violates least privilege.

options:
Add a targeted allow for the Lambda role without the IP condition:
```json
{
  "Sid": "LambdaException",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/ingestor-lambda"},
  "Action": ["s3:PutObject"],
  "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::example-bucket/*"
}
```

Detach the bucket policy and instead attach this identity policy to the Lambda role:
```json
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": ["s3:PutObject"],
  "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::example-bucket/*"
}
```
concept_mcqs.explanation: An additional Allow for the specific Lambda role bypasses the IP condition for that principal only. With no explicit Deny present, the request is authorized for that role and remains restricted by IP for all other principals.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B: Identity-based allows cannot override a bucket policy’s restrictions if the bucket policy does not grant access; the request is still implicitly denied. C: `aws:ViaAWSService` does not apply to direct S3 API calls made by a role; it applies when a service calls on your behalf. D: User agent strings are not a reliable or recommended control and can be spoofed; also S3 does not expose it as a policy key for authorization.

Regioned EC2/S3 calls set the key and are denied. STS requests generally resolve to a region (global or regional endpoint) and will be denied when the resolved region is not in the allowed list.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B and C: Both are region-scoped and set `aws:RequestedRegion` to us-east-1, which fails the condition and triggers the Deny. D: STS requests resolve to a region; using the global endpoint typically maps to us-east-1 and will be denied by the guardrail.

concept_mcqs.stem:
Change ticket for CVE-XXXX-YYYY mitigation reads:
```text
1) EC2 web fleet (Amazon Linux 2): wait for AWS to patch the OS on our instances
2) Amazon RDS MySQL: rely on AWS to patch the underlying OS
3) AWS Lambda runtimes: rely on AWS to patch the managed runtime
4) S3 buckets: ensure server-side encryption is configured per company policy
```
Which line misassigns responsibility under the shared responsibility model?
options: 3) AWS Lambda runtimes: rely on AWS to patch the managed runtime
1) EC2 web fleet (Amazon Linux 2): wait for AWS to patch the OS on our instances
2) Amazon RDS MySQL: rely on AWS to patch the underlying OS
4) S3 buckets: ensure server-side encryption is configured per company policy
concept_mcqs.explanation: On EC2, the customer is responsible for OS-level patching inside the instance. AWS patches the hypervisor and underlying infrastructure. RDS OS patching and Lambda runtime patching are AWS responsibilities, while configuring S3 encryption to meet policy is the customer's responsibility.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B: For RDS, AWS manages the underlying OS; customers patch at the engine-level per maintenance window. C: AWS manages the Lambda runtime environment. D: Customers must configure S3 encryption; this is correctly assigned to the customer.

options: Add an extra Allow for `ec2:StartInstances` to the user to override the Deny.
Use long-lived access keys with the AWS CLI to bypass console MFA prompts.
Sign in with MFA and obtain a session where `aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent` is true.
Remove the Deny and keep only Allows on required actions.
concept_mcqs.explanation: The explicit Deny based on `aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent` overrides any Allows. The correct fix is to meet the condition by authenticating with MFA.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B: Removing the Deny weakens enforcement and violates the requirement. C: Explicit Deny takes precedence over Allows; it will not override. D: Long-lived keys are still subject to the same condition; using them without MFA remains denied.

concept_mcqs.stem:
User `dev1` has an inline policy and is in group `Viewers`.
Inline user policy:
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{"Effect": "Allow", "Action": "ec2:*", "Resource": "*"}]
}
```
Group `Viewers` policy:
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{"Effect": "Deny", "Action": "ec2:TerminateInstances", "Resource": "*"}]
}
```
What happens when `dev1` runs `aws ec2 terminate-instances --instance-ids i-0123456789abcdef0`?
options: Allowed only if the instance has a specific tag permitting termination.
Allowed, because user inline policies take precedence over group policies.
Allowed, but only in the region where the user was created.
Denied, because explicit Deny in any applicable policy overrides Allows.
concept_mcqs.explanation: An explicit Deny in any applicable policy (user, group, boundary, or session) overrides all Allows. The terminate action is denied.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: A: There is no precedence where user inline beats group; evaluation considers all policies and Deny wins. B: IAM users are global; region of creation is irrelevant. D: No tag condition exists in the provided policies; introducing one would be a different configuration.

concept_mcqs.stem:
An EC2 instance with an attached instance profile cannot get credentials:
```bash
curl -s http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/
# returns empty
```
Role trust policy:
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect": "Allow", "Principal": {"AWS": "*"}, "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"}
  ]
}
```
Which change is required for the instance to receive role credentials via IMDS?
options: Use long-term access keys on the instance profile instead of a role.
Add an inline policy to the role allowing `sts:GetSessionToken`.
Attach an identity policy allowing `sts:AssumeRole` to the EC2 instance.
concept_mcqs.explanation: For EC2 instances to assume a role via the instance profile, the role's trust policy must trust the EC2 service principal `ec2.amazonaws.com`.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: A: Instances don’t have identities that can hold identity policies; the instance role is assumed by the EC2 service. B: `GetSessionToken` is irrelevant; the issue is trust, not permissions. C: Long-term keys on an instance defeat the purpose of roles and do not integrate with IMDS.

concept_mcqs.stem:
You try to restrict DescribeInstances to a specific instance:
Policy attached to user:
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Action": ["ec2:DescribeInstances"],
    "Resource": ["arn:aws:ec2:us-east-1:111122223333:instance/i-0123456789abcdef0"]
  }]
}
```
Command:
```bash
aws ec2 describe-instances --instance-ids i-0123456789abcdef0 --region us-east-1
```
Result: AccessDenied. Why, and what change fixes it without over-broadening?
options: The instance ARN is missing a wildcard; change it to `...:instance/*`.
Use `ec2:GetInstance` instead of `DescribeInstances` to target a single ARN.
DescribeInstances does not support resource-level permissions; set `"Resource": "*"` and rely on request parameters to scope results.
Switch to the `ec2:ListInstances` action which supports ARNs.
concept_mcqs.explanation: Many EC2 Describe/List actions are not resource-level and require `Resource: *`. You must allow the action broadly and scope with request parameters on the client side.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B: Wildcards don't help when the action itself is not resource-scoped. C and D: These actions do not exist; the correct action is DescribeInstances.

concept_mcqs.stem: You need a policy to prevent resource creation outside `eu-west-1` and `eu-central-1` without breaking global services. Pick the best statement to attach alongside existing Allows.
concept_mcqs.explanation: Using Deny with `StringNotEqualsIfExists` avoids impacting calls where the key is not set, and `NotAction` exempts global services that should remain usable. This is a common pattern for region guardrails without collateral damage.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: A: Without IfExists or exemptions, global services may be inadvertently blocked. C: `aws:Region` is not a valid condition key. D: Relying only on Allows is bypassable by other Allows and does not create a hard guardrail.

concept_mcqs.stem:
You attach this policy to enforce tag-on-create for cost allocation:
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{
    "Sid": "DenyWithoutCostCenter",
    "Effect": "Deny",
    "Action": ["ec2:RunInstances"],
    "Resource": "*",
    "Condition": {"Null": {"aws:RequestTag/CostCenter": "true"}}
  }]
}
```
A developer runs:
```bash
aws ec2 run-instances \
  --image-id ami-1234567890abcdef0 \
  --instance-type t3.micro \
  --region eu-west-1
```
What happens and why?
options: The deny applies to console launches only; CLI calls are unaffected.
The launch is allowed only in eu-west-1 due to the organization’s region guardrail.
The launch succeeds; the instance can be tagged later to satisfy cost allocation.
The launch is denied until the developer supplies a `CostCenter` tag in the request.
concept_mcqs.explanation: The `Null` condition denies when the request does not include the required tag key at create time, enforcing least privilege and governance at the API boundary.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B: This policy enforces tag-on-create; post-creation tagging does not satisfy the condition. C: The policy shown is not region-scoped; region guardrails would be separate. D: IAM policies apply uniformly to API calls regardless of console or CLI.

scenario_questions.scenario: A vendor’s CI system in Account A must deploy CloudFormation stacks to your Account B only in EU regions to meet data residency commitments and contain spend. Auditors also require that no deployments occur outside `eu-west-1` or `eu-central-1`, and that long-lived credentials are not issued to the vendor.
scenario_questions.task: Design the access pattern and controls. Specify the IAM role, trust policy (including any external ID), session configuration, and guardrail policy needed to restrict regions while preserving the vendor’s ability to deploy in the two allowed regions. Justify each design choice in terms of least privilege and shared responsibility.
scenario_questions.expected_answer: Propose a cross-account role `DeployEUOnly` in Account B with a trust policy that names only the vendor’s principal (their CI role or user) and requires a specific `sts:ExternalId`. Limit the assume role session duration (e.g., 1 hour) and consider `sts:TagSession` for traceability. Attach to the role a permissions policy that allows only the CloudFormation/related actions required. Add a separate Deny statement using `StringNotEqualsIfExists` on `aws:RequestedRegion` to enforce region restriction, optionally with `NotAction` exempting IAM/Route53/etc. Show example trust and permissions policy JSON. Explain why roles (ephemeral credentials) satisfy the no-long-lived-keys requirement, and how region guardrails reduce risk/cost. Note IAM’s global scope and how `IfExists` avoids breaking global services. Mention logging (CloudTrail) and conditions like `aws:PrincipalArn` or external ID to prevent confused-deputy problems.

rubric.criterion: Correctly proposes role-based cross-account access (no long-lived keys) with a precise Principal and ExternalId in trust policy
Includes and correctly explains a region guardrail using `aws:RequestedRegion` with IfExists and appropriate exemptions
Outlines least-privilege permissions for deployment (scoped actions/resources) and short session duration
Explains reasoning tied to shared responsibility, risk reduction, and auditability (e.g., session tags/CloudTrail)

scenario_questions.scenario: Your security scanner flags that an S3 bucket with customer PDFs is publicly readable. The platform team says, “AWS made it public.” The bucket was created two years ago. You must restore least privilege and document responsibility boundaries and corrective actions.
scenario_questions.task: Write what actually caused the exposure under IAM’s evaluation logic and shared responsibility, then propose a concrete remediation plan and verifiable checks to prove closure. Your plan must avoid breaking existing producers that write into the bucket from a VPC.
scenario_questions.expected_answer: Cause is customer-side misconfiguration: a public bucket policy and/or ACL, not AWS. Under shared responsibility, AWS secures the infrastructure; customers configure access policies. Remediation: enable and enforce S3 Block Public Access at the account and bucket level; remove public ACLs and any `Principal: *` Allows; keep required access via specific principals (roles) and/or VPC endpoints. Add a bucket policy that allows only specific role ARNs and denies non-VPC endpoint access if using Gateway Endpoint (Condition on `aws:SourceVpce`), leaving producers unaffected. Verification: Access Analyzer finding resolved; `aws s3api get-bucket-policy-status` shows not public; attempt unauthenticated GET fails; authenticated role PUT still succeeds; CloudTrail shows only authorized principals. Document the controls and who owns them.

rubric.criterion: Correctly attributes responsibility to customer configuration and explains IAM evaluation (public policy/ACL) rather than AWS fault
Concrete remediation steps including Block Public Access, policy/ACL fixes, and principal-specific access that preserves producer flows
Verifiable checks (Access Analyzer status, CLI/API evidence of deny to public and allow to producers)

scenario_questions.scenario: Your company mandates MFA for all human administrators, but an automation role used by a deployment pipeline is failing because of an account-wide policy that denies actions when `aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent` is false.
scenario_questions.task: Propose a corrected policy design that enforces MFA for humans without blocking non-interactive automation roles. Describe how you will separate or target the controls, and provide policy snippets that demonstrate the change. Explain trade-offs and how you will prove it works.
scenario_questions.expected_answer: Separate human users from automation by identity (e.g., put human users in a `Humans` group; automation uses roles). Attach an explicit Deny to the `Humans` group that triggers only for users: use a condition targeting user principals (e.g., scope by Principal ARN pattern `arn:aws:iam::*:user/*`, or better, require a principal tag `Type=Human` and enforce tagging with a permission boundary or provisioning process). Example Deny: Effect Deny, Action `*`, Resource `*`, Condition `BoolIfExists` on `aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent=false`, combined with `StringLike` `aws:PrincipalArn` for `*:user/*`. Exempt roles by not attaching the Deny to them (or add a Condition that requires `aws:PrincipalTag/Type=Human=true`). Validate: console/API calls by tagged users without MFA are denied; the pipeline role executes when assuming the role without MFA. Log evidence via CloudTrail and test calls.

rubric.criterion: Clear separation strategy between human users and automation roles (groups, tags, or both)
Correct IAM condition targeting (Principal pattern/tag) and MFA-based Deny that does not impact roles
Test/verification plan demonstrating both enforcement for humans and non-impact for automation
Discussion of least privilege and operational trade-offs (e.g., tagging governance, boundary use)

scenario_questions.scenario: A new customer portal must meet a 99.9% monthly availability target, keep EU customer data in-region, and avoid surprise bills during a pilot. There is no cross-region DR requirement for the pilot; business traffic is mostly in Ireland and Germany.
scenario_questions.task: Choose a region/AZ strategy, identify which controls are yours vs AWS under shared responsibility, and name price levers you will consciously set at launch. Deliver a concise architecture note outline with justifications.
scenario_questions.expected_answer: Pick a single EU region with multi-AZ for the pilot, e.g., `eu-west-1` (Ireland) for latency to Irish users, optionally `eu-central-1` if nearer to Germany, stating rationale. Use at least two AZs for stateful tiers to hit 99.9% with managed services that support multi-AZ. Data residency: ensure all data stores and backups remain in-region; restrict regions with an organization/user policy using `aws:RequestedRegion` IfExists pattern. Shared responsibility: customer configures IAM, encryption, patching on EC2, backup strategy; AWS operates facilities, AZ isolation, managed service substrates. Price levers: choose right-size instance types or serverless, enable multi-AZ only where needed, use on-demand for pilot, set budgets/alerts, and avoid cross-AZ chatter where not required. Include brief notes on monitoring and rollback.

rubric.criterion: Region and AZ choice tied to availability target and EU residency, with clear justification
Shared responsibility delineation listing at least three customer controls (IAM, patching, encryption/backups) vs AWS responsibilities
Concrete price levers (instance class/serverless choice, on-demand vs commitment, cross-AZ traffic awareness, budgets)
Explicit region guardrail mention to prevent drift, and operational considerations (monitoring/rollback)

practical_tasks.title: Architecture note: EU-resident pilot with 99.9% availability and spend guardrails
practical_tasks.brief: Produce a 1–2 page architecture note for a simple web application pilot that must keep data in the EU, meet 99.9% availability, and avoid accidental spend in non-EU regions. Focus on region/AZ choice, shared responsibility controls, and price levers. Include any IAM guardrail snippets you propose.
